title: Journey-aware telemetry enrichment and read-optimized trace slices
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Add a lightweight enrichment layer and storage pattern to make analytics ingest traces journey-aware and query-efficient. Goals: (1) attach deterministic journey IDs to multi-request flows without requiring downstream code changes, (2) capture read-optimized 'trace slices' for analytics pipelines that reduce storage and query cost while preserving root-cause details for SLO violations, and (3) integrate per-tenant budgeted capture and long-tail-preserving sampling so we maintain signal for rare errors.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic journey ID added to analytics events for >95% of ingestion flows without client changes (computed from stable headers + event fingerprints)
Trace slice schema defined and stored in S3/Parquet with 4x smaller average size than full traces for normal flows, retention queryable from console dashboards
Per-tenant daily trace capture budget enforced (configurable), with graceful degradation and fallback logs when budget exceeded
SLO dashboard shows journey-level SLIs (p99 latency, error-rate) computed from enriched events and aligns with sampled trace slices for at least 90% of incidents in the test window
End-to-end test demonstrating long-tail error preservation: errors with frequency <0.01% are captured at >90% probability for 30 days
proposal: Introduce a telemetry enrichment proxy that sits between ingestion edge and analytics ingest. The proxy computes a JourneyID using a deterministic function (stable header priorities, request hashing, session cookie fallback) and annotates events. Parallelly, emit a lightweight "trace slice" that retains request headers, service hop summary, timing buckets, and the last N log frames (configurable) instead of full verbose spans. Store slices in columnar format with partitioning by JourneyID date and tenant for fast S3 queries. Implement a budget controller service that counts daily trace-slice bytes per tenant and triggers tiered sampling policies (head-preserve, error-prioritized, reservoir for rare events).
design_decisions: Use deterministic JourneyID rather than centralized session store to avoid cross-tenant coordination and keep latency low
Trace slices are canonicalized to Parquet with a fixed column set to enable predicate pushdown in analytics queries
Sampling policy uses a two-pass approach: 1) error-first capture (retain all error codes), 2) head-preserve for first N requests of a journey, 3) reservoir sampling for low-frequency tails
Do not change existing public event schema; enrichment adds optional metadata fields (journey_id, slice_ref) to avoid client migrations
implementation_notes: Work split across three sub-tasks: (A) Telemetry proxy (Go) that enriches and emits slice refs; (B) Slice writer service that performs canonicalization and writes Parquet to S3 with tenant/day partitions; (C) Budget controller and sampling service (Python) with Redis-based counters and fairness heuristics. Add feature flags for gradual rollout and per-tenant overrides. Instrument both proxy and writer with SLIs (ingest latency, slicing success rate, write size distribution).
test_plan: Unit tests for JourneyID determinism across header permutations. Integration tests with a synthetic traffic generator to validate size reduction and correctness. Chaos test: simulate proxy drop and ensure analytics falls back to original events without slice metadata. Perf test: measure added latency <5ms p50 at 95th percentile under 10k rps. Data validation job to compare SLI calculations from raw event baseline vs enriched slices over a one-week window.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary 5 tenants with non-critical traffic behind a feature flag (1 week). 2) Monitor ingestion latency, slice write errors, budget throttle rate for 72 hours. 3) Expand to 25 tenants and run SLI correlation tests. 4) Gradual enable for all tenants with opt-out for those who want no enrichment. Provide runbook for rollback (disable proxy enrichment flag and delete slice writer config to stop full writes).
monitoring_queries: SLO: journey_p99_latency = 100 * (count(journey_latency_ms > p99_threshold) / count(journeys)) — computed daily
Budget throttle rate: sum(slice_throttle_count) by tenant over 1d / sum(slice_attempts) by tenant over 1d
Slice size distribution: histogram(slice_bytes) by tenant to monitor storage regression
Error preservation check: ratio(captured_error_events / observed_error_events) over 7d (goal >0.9)
Ingest latency impact: p50/p95 of proxy_additional_ms compared to baseline
